videos.title: VoiceOver sigue abriendo puertas. Phonon trae nuevas voces a la conversación
videos.description:
VoiceOver continúa ampliando sus posibilidades, y hoy le toca el turno a Phonon, una aplicación que permite incorporar nuevas voces al lector de pantalla de Apple.
En este tutorial conoceremos cómo funciona Phonon, cómo explorar las voces disponibles, seleccionar las que nos interesan, descargarlas y utilizarlas con VoiceOver.
Todo explicado paso a paso, con demostraciones prácticas para que puedan escuchar las voces y valorar cuáles se ajustan mejor a sus preferencias.
Porque cuando hablamos de accesibilidad, tener más opciones para elegir siempre es una buena noticia.

videos.title: ¿Una galería de fotos pensada para personas ciegas? Así funciona Memora
videos.description:
Memora: ¿para qué quiere una persona ciega una galería de fotos?
¿Quién dijo que las fotografías son solamente para quienes pueden verlas?
Hoy les presento Memora, una aplicación para iPhone desarrollada por un programador ciego que propone una forma accesible de explorar y organizar nuestras fotografías.
En este tutorial recorreremos sus principales funciones, comprobaremos cómo se maneja con VoiceOver y veremos qué posibilidades ofrece en la práctica.
Una nueva oportunidad para demostrar que la accesibilidad también tiene mucho que decir en el mundo de la fotografía.
TifloAcosta. Tecnología al alcance de todos.

videos.title: Apple te quiere… proteger. ¡Pero tienes que activarlo! iOS 27
videos.description:
Apple quiere protegernos de las estafas, y con iOS 27 incorpora una nueva función llamada «Detección de riesgo de suplantación de identidad».
¿En qué consiste? ¿Puede nuestro iPhone detectar que alguien está intentando engañarnos para conseguir nuestro dinero o nuestros datos personales?
En este vídeo de TifloAcosta explico cómo funciona esta protección, cuáles son sus limitaciones y cómo podemos activarla desde los ajustes del iPhone utilizando VoiceOver.
Una novedad importante que viene desactivada de fábrica y que necesita aplicaciones compatibles para funcionar. No evita todas las estafas, pero puede aportar una protección adicional.

videos.title: Yo ya no persigo las noticias: ahora vienen a buscarme
videos.description:
En este vídeo les presento cMRSS, una aplicación accesible que permite reunir en un mismo lugar las fuentes de noticias y contenidos que realmente nos
interesan.
Podemos añadir medios y páginas mediante sus fuentes RSS, organizar lo que seguimos y consultar las novedades sin tener que ir saltando de una web a otra.
Pero hay una función que a mí me ha gustado especialmente: también podemos añadir canales de YouTube y seguir sus nuevas publicaciones desde la propia
aplicación, sin necesidad de entrar continuamente en YouTube para comprobar qué han publicado.
cMRSS no es gratuita, y eso también hay que decirlo. Pero después de usarla y comprobar lo que me ofrece, en mi caso considero que merece la pena la inversión.
En el vídeo les enseño cómo funciona, qué posibilidades ofrece y por qué se ha ganado un sitio entre las aplicaciones que utilizo para mantenerme informado.

videos.title: TifloAcosta ya tiene app: todo cambia a partir de aquí
videos.description:
TIFLOACOSTA APP — ACCESO DIRECTO
Este enlace abre directamente TifloAcosta App. No necesitas descargar ningún archivo ni registrarte para entrar. Desde ahí puedes utilizar la aplicación en el navegador y, si quieres, instalarla en tu dispositivo para tenerla disponible como una app más.
TifloAcosta da hoy uno de los pasos más importantes desde que comenzó este proyecto.
Durante mucho tiempo hemos ido creando vídeos, cursos, guías, documentos, recursos en español y en inglés y una comunidad que sigue creciendo. El problema es que todo ese material estaba repartido entre distintos lugares.
Ha llegado el momento de empezar a reunirlo.
TifloAcosta ya tiene su propia app.
Desde ella puedes buscar recursos por palabras, recorrerlos por categorías, consultar las novedades, guardar tus favoritos y acceder al catálogo completo de vídeos del Canal TifloAcosta.
Además, la aplicación se ha pensado desde el principio teniendo en cuenta la accesibilidad y el uso con lectores de pantalla.
En este vídeo te enseño cómo funciona, qué puedes encontrar dentro y cómo puedes instalarla para tener TifloAcosta mucho más cerca.
La demostración práctica se realiza en iPhone utilizando VoiceOver, y también explico cómo acceder e instalarla desde Android y Windows.
Si quieres entrar directamente mientras ves el vídeo, este es nuevamente el enlace:
La aplicación seguirá creciendo.
Iremos incorporando nuevos recursos, mejorando lo que ya existe y ajustando aquello que la experiencia real de los usuarios nos vaya indicando.
Porque esto no pretende ser simplemente otra página donde acumular enlaces.
La idea es mucho más ambiciosa: crear un lugar estable, accesible y sencillo desde el que entrar a todo lo que TifloAcosta va construyendo.
Hasta ahora, TifloAcosta era principalmente un canal, una comunidad y una colección de contenidos repartidos por distintos espacios.
Desde hoy empieza a tener su propia casa.
Y acabamos de abrir la puerta.

videos.title: Este atajo no pregunta, ve un código y se pone a investigar
videos.description:
Ponle un código delante… y a ver qué pasa
Hoy les traigo uno de esos atajos que empiezas haciendo para resolver una cosa y al final termina haciendo bastante más de lo previsto.
La idea es sencilla: encontrar un código y averiguar qué contiene.
Puede trabajar con códigos que estén en una imagen o una captura guardada en el iPhone, pero también con códigos que tengamos delante y podamos captar con la cámara.
Y no nos quedamos únicamente con los códigos QR.
El atajo también puede reconocer códigos de barras y, cuando encuentra información que merece la pena investigar, utiliza Internet para intentar averiguar qué hay detrás de ese código y ofrecernos información útil.
Por ejemplo, podemos encontrarnos un código de barras en un producto y querer saber qué es, o recibir una imagen que contiene un QR sin tener otro teléfono disponible para escanearlo.
La intención ha sido precisamente esa: tener una herramienta sencilla y accesible que podamos lanzar desde el iPhone y dejar que haga el trabajo.
En el vídeo les enseño cómo funciona y las distintas posibilidades que ofrece.
IMPORTANTE:
Para utilizar este atajo es necesario tener instalada la aplicación gratuita Actions, ya que algunas de las funciones que utiliza el atajo proceden de esta aplicación.
Descargar Actions desde la App Store:
Instalar el atajo:
Una vez instalada Actions, conviene abrirla al menos una vez. Si sus acciones no aparecen posteriormente en la aplicación Atajos, reinicien el iPhone.
Como siempre, este atajo lo comparto para que puedan probarlo, jugar con él y, sobre todo, sacarle partido.
Tony Acosta
Canal TifloAcosta

El atajo también puede reconocer códigos de barras y, cuando encuentra información que merece la pena investigar, utiliza Internet para intentar averiguar qué hay detrás de ese código y ofrecernos información útil.

Por ejemplo, podemos encontrarnos un código de barras en un producto y querer saber qué es, o recibir una imagen que contiene un QR sin tener otro teléfono disponible para escanearlo.

La intención ha sido precisamente esa: tener una herramienta sencilla y accesible que podamos lanzar desde el iPhone y dejar que haga el trabajo.

En el vídeo les enseño cómo funciona y las distintas posibilidades que ofrece.

IMPORTANTE:

Para utilizar este atajo es necesario tener instalada la aplicación gratuita Actions, ya que algunas de las funciones que utiliza el atajo proceden de esta aplicación.

https://apps.apple.com/es/app/actions/id1586435171

Instalar el atajo:
https://www.icloud.com/shortcuts/477bfbed55a84c1aa568b748acd638de

Una vez instalada Actions, conviene abrirla al menos una vez. Si sus acciones no aparecen posteriormente en la aplicación Atajos, reinicien el iPhone.

Como siempre, este atajo lo comparto para que puedan probarlo, jugar con él y, sobre todo, sacarle partido.

videos.title: Actualizaciones invisibles en iPhone: qué son y por qué importan
videos.description:
Apple no solo actualiza el iPhone cuando aparece una nueva versión de iOS. Existe un sistema menos visible que trabaja en segundo plano y que mucha gente no conoce: las actualizaciones rápidas de seguridad y datos del sistema.
Estas actualizaciones no requieren descargar una versión completa del sistema ni reiniciar el dispositivo. Se aplican de forma automática y están diseñadas para corregir fallos de seguridad urgentes, actualizar bases de datos internas o mejorar el funcionamiento de servicios clave.
Se encuentran dentro de Ajustes, General, Actualización de software, y dependen de una opción llamada “Respuestas de seguridad y archivos del sistema”. Si está activada, el iPhone puede recibir mejoras sin que el usuario tenga que hacer nada.
En este vídeo se explica qué son exactamente estas actualizaciones, qué cambian en el dispositivo, por qué Apple las utiliza cada vez más y qué ventajas tienen frente a las actualizaciones tradicionales de iOS.
videos.fullDescription:

news.title: Why you should never vacuum the inside of your computer
news.summary: Ensuring that your PC is dust free is key, but taking a vacuum to your motherboard and other components can be very damaging. Here's what you should do instead.
news.body:
A quick clean could result in a lot of damage.

Dust: the enemy hiding in every PC case. It clogs vents and builds up between heatsink fins, making it harder for your PC's fans to keep things cool. Naturally, you'll want to clean it out. Dealing with debris almost anywhere else in your home, you'd reach for your vacuum cleaner. It's got the power to clean it all out, with narrow attachments to reach in those awkward gaps and corners.

Bringing a vacuum cleaner to clean inside your computer is like bringing a pressure washer to clean a painting. You might clear the dirt, but you risk damaging what you're trying to clean. With sensitive (and expensive) components inside, it's not just physical damage you have to worry about. You've got static to worry about, too. There are better ways to clean your PC case, so if you're thinking about grabbing your vacuum, there are good reasons why you should really give it a miss.

Have you ever felt an electric shock after you've walked across a carpet and touched something metal? That's an electrostatic discharge: a buildup of electric charge finding a path to somewhere with unequal electrical potential. A small, momentary annoyance for you, but inside your PC, even a discharge too small for you to feel can damage sensitive components.

A household vacuum can build up static as dust and other particles travel through its hose, particularly around plastic parts. If you bring the nozzle close to the components inside your PC, that charge is then able to transfer into them.

There are no guarantees. You might get lucky with no damage. Alternatively, your first attempt might be catastrophic. Unfortunately, there's just no way to prevent (or estimate) such outcomes. Electrostatic damage can cause immediate failures, but it can also detrimentally affect a component without you initially realizing. Given how expensive a PC can be, especially high-end gaming PCs, it likely isn't ever worth the risk.

There's an exception, though. You can buy specialist vacuums that are designed to work with static-sensitive electronics. These aren't the same as the household cleaners you're using on your carpets and rugs. They're usually built with materials in the hose and attachments that allow static charge to dissipate rather than accumulate. It'll give that charge a path to safely ground rather than build up around the nozzle, where it could come into contact with your PC.

While static is a big risk, there are other factors involved. Bluntly, a vacuum cleaner is a fairly clumsy tool. In a PC case, especially a small one, there isn't a lot of space to move around. There are cables to think about, along with exposed components that you don't really want to catch with the nozzle. It's very easy to knock a connector off while trying to reach a patch of dust, particularly if the hose is blocking your view.

You may also use attachments. Brush attachments, for instance, might catch on small parts. A hard nozzle could strike against a circuit board or bend small fins on a heatsink. Then there are loose screws; if any drop inside your case, then a vacuum will whisk them away.

You'll have to think particularly carefully about the fans, too. Air pulled through by a vacuum can make the blades spin. Forcing this to happen rapidly can put unnecessary stress on its bearings, but there's also the potential of physical damage.

Laptops don't give you much room to work with, either. You could shove a vacuum nozzle against the cooling vents to clean your laptop fans , but you can't see what's happening inside or hold the fan still to stop the suction from spinning it. If dust has built up between the fan and the heatsink fins, you may need to remove the bottom cover to reach it, if your model allows it. The same advice applies, though: a laptop is just a more compact PC, and a vacuum won't be any safer inside one.

With any luck, you've now been warned off from putting vacuum inside your PC (unless it's a specialized, anti-static one). There are simply too many downsides and too many risks. There are many better options, too. A can of compressed air, or an electric air duster designed for electronics, can help you quickly blow dust out of a PC case.

Whatever you do, you'll want to start by switching your PC off and disconnecting it from an outlet. Take out the external power cables and, if you can, move it somewhere clean. Ideally, somewhere with plenty of air flow, especially if you're using air to blast out the dust. If you can't, use a mask if you have one spare, and make sure to open plenty of windows.

Compressed air is your friend when it comes to PC cleaning. Compressed air cans, or an electric air duster, is a static-free alternative to vacuuming. You're pushing air through the case with enough force to clean the dust out. Short bursts are best, just so you can control where you're directing the air without sending dust further into the case. They're particularly useful for cleaning out any clumps of dust stuck deep inside.

There's no special knack to this; you'll just want to use your judgement. Where you can, you might want to try and hold fan blades still while cleaning around them, especially if you're using an electric duster with a lot of power. You've still got to be careful with delicate components, so don't push tools blindly or force a nozzle into a gap you can't see into. Any inaccessible areas should be considered with care. The same applies to your power supply, too. You don't want to open that up , as its internal components can retain dangerous electrical charges, although you can clear surface dust from its external fan grill without reaching inside.

If you're lucky, your PC might have removable dust filters that you can clean separately. These might sit in front of your case fans as a way to block some of the dust entering. If you're able to remove them, pull them out and give them a thorough clean. A damp cloth should work, but keep moisture away from any circuit boards and let the filters dry completely before you reinstall them. You can use a dry microfiber cloth to wipe down the outside of the case, too.

When you're done, double-check everything inside. Internal cables should be securely connected, with none trailing into the fan blades. Once your case is clean, you'll be in a better position to keep it that way. Keep it off the floor if you can , too, as it'll help to reduce the amount of dust you're drawing in through your fans. You can't stop dust completely, but you can keep it manageable enough, with occasional checks and cleans in place, before it starts clogging up your vents again.

news.title: Can you completely remove One UI from a Samsung phone?
news.summary: Samsung's custom software, One UI, gives every phone a similar appearance. Discover how to limit One UI and change the look of your homepage.
news.body:
No, but there are ways to make One UI less prominent.

Samsung's One UI is a staple feature of the company's phones and tablets, and for most users, it handles everything well enough. That doesn't mean it's perfect, though, and there are plenty of reasons why you might want to replace it with another set of apps entirely. The bad news is that you can't remove One UI from a Samsung phone, but there are ways to cut out the parts you find frustrating or unhelpful with just a little effort.

First, it's important to understand what One UI actually is and the features it offers . One UI is custom software for Samsung phones, but in many cases, what people actually want to change is their launcher, which determines the look of the home screen. While that's part of the picture, One UI also encompasses a set of features and pre-installed apps that affect every aspect of your phone. Some parts of One UI will always be running on a Samsung phone, but replacing your launcher and removing other apps can help get the results you want without switching phones entirely.

Switching out your launcher will have the biggest impact on how your phone looks and behaves. Fortunately, it's extremely easy to change, since launchers can be downloaded from the Play Store like any other app. Once you've downloaded a new launcher, just open the Settings app, tap the Apps menu, then Choose default apps . Make sure you set your new launcher under Home app and it should automatically replace One UI Home when you open your phone.

Niagara Launcher and Smart Launcher are among the most popular third-party launchers for Android, but there are plenty of other options out there. If you'd rather keep the home screen but tune it to your liking, Samsung even offers its own solution for customizing your phone with One UI 9 . The Good Lock app isn't an entirely new launcher, but it offers tons of customization settings that can change your home screen so much it might solve your One UI woes in the same way.

Even if you're happy with One UI , it's still packed with apps you might be better off without. By default, One UI includes a suite of apps to handle basic functions covering everything from health tracking to a digital wallet. While they're perfectly serviceable, there are plenty of other apps out there that do the same things, and there's no reason to keep the built-in options if you're not using them.

Since they're system apps, most of these can't be completely deleted, but you can hide them and limit how much space they take up on your phone. First, head to Settings , then Apps and type Samsung into the search bar. Tap the option you want to remove. Some, like Notes, allow you to uninstall them completely. If there's no uninstall option, tap the three dots menu in the top right and select Uninstall updates . The app will remain, but it won't take up as much storage space.

Once you've done that, you can also keep the icons of remaining apps from cluttering up your phone. In Settings , head to Home screen , then scroll down to Hide apps on Home and Apps screen . Then, just select the apps you don't want to see and they'll be hidden. It's an imperfect solution for sure, but it can help make your phone much easier to navigate.

news.title: The purpose of the SC port on your old laptop
news.summary: If you have a weird, credit-card-sized slot on your laptop, read on to find out what it's for and how it's used.
news.body:
No, it can't process a credit card payment for an online purchase.

The laptop market is an interesting one, in that while there's certainly a compelling history of its competition with desktop PCs, in the end, these two categories diverged to meet different needs. More recently, the desktop PC market has been defined by prebuilt systems and custom builds focused on gaming and entertainment, but the laptop scene still feels very business-like.

One aspect of laptop design that has contributed to this feeling for decades now is the collection of unique features that have come and gone. In particular, the SC slot, also known as the smart card reader.

The SC port isn't likely to be on a laptop you walk out of Best Buy or Target with, but its use cases are often quite amusing for those who don't need one. If you do happen to have a laptop with an SC port, chances are you are a professional with an important job or bought something secondhand, leaving you wondering exactly what this unusual port can actually do.

A smart card reader does exactly what it sounds like. It's designed to read and interact with cards of various kinds — often the kind of security and ID badges you might see dangling from the lanyard of a corporate employee. The readers are mostly found on business laptops, where the main goal of the machine is to facilitate an efficient workflow as opposed to watching YouTube videos.

Government agencies and security companies make use of smart card readers to maintain a stronger sense of control over their potentially sensitive information. It's not a perfect system, but even one extra layer of protection can make a world of difference.

They're also common on school-issued laptops, as students can use them to gain access to private portals for assignments or schedules. While a reader has the potential to make a user feel like a secret agent of some kind as they insert a card to gain access to sensitive information, the average person isn't likely to use one, or indeed even have an SC port on their laptop.

The core concept of a device that can read these cards isn't exclusive to laptops , of course. The technology is what we use every day when we check out at stores and insert cards into a machine, and standalone units designed for small businesses have existed for decades in the form of POS, or point-of-sale, systems.

If your laptop does happen to have a smart card reader, however, you may be wondering if you have any actual use for it. While it would be fun to be able to actually insert a credit or debit card in it to pay for something online, none of them can actually complete transactions. In reality, there are very few genuine uses that your average, everyday person would have for a smart card reader in a laptop.

If you are an incredibly security-fixated person, it's possible but impractical to use the smart card reader to create an extra layer of security on a home laptop. It's remarkably complex, and for most people, a simple two-factor authentication will work just fine.

news.title: Word Burner: Daily Chain
news.summary: A daily word chain against the clock. Every word starts on the last letter of the one before, and every letter you start a word with burns. Land on a burnt letter and the fire goes out. Everyone gets the same puzzle each day, and you get one scored run. Two minutes. How far can you chain? news.title: Tact: Find It by Touch
news.summary: A haptic game you play by touch, without looking at the screen. The screen is black glass. Feel for the one place that is different, and break it. Tap anywhere with one to five fingers, the way you'd play a piano. Each tap answers with a small tick under your fingertip. Somewhere, one place feels different: a little longer, a double tap, or a little harder. When you find it, keep tapping it. A crack runs across the glass, and it breaks, with a deep haptic, a short high glass sound and a soft light. Play it absent-mindedly, with the TV on. Each pane you break still feels like a small win. While you play, no score appears on screen. Numbers show only when you pause, when a Time Attack run ends, or when a pane breaks in a Duel. FOUR WAYS TO PLAY • Calm: No time limit, no score. Find the one place that feels different, and keep breaking the glass • Standard: Each pane you break makes the difference a little subtler (12 levels). If you can't find it, it becomes clearer again. Pause to see your current level and your best • Time Attack: How many panes can you break while the line goes once around the screen in 60 seconds? Cues at the start, every 15 seconds and in the last 3 seconds. Your best is kept • Duel: Two players, one iPhone laid between you, face to face. Each of you has a place of your own that feels different (longer or double tap). Whoever's place breaks first scores, even if the other player broke it. First to 1, 3, 5 or 7 RECORDS • Your best level in Standard and your best count in Time Attack • Records made with Stronger Difference or Sound Hints on are kept apart as assisted records MAKE IT YOURS • Haptic Strength: Gentle, Standard or Strong • Sound volume, and Tap Sound • Touch Trace, and Completion Light (Off, Soft or Bright) • Taps to Break: 5, 7, 10 or 12 (10 to start) • Settings are under the faint gear that appears at the top right when you pause. While playing, hold two fingers for two seconds, then lift them GETTING STARTED • On first launch, a short tutorial of about 30 seconds, on a bigger 2×3 grid • Watch it again any time with Replay Tutorial in Settings FOR EVERYONE • Playable with VoiceOver. The play area takes your taps directly, and the tutorial text, the time left and results in Time Attack, level changes, and points and wins in a Duel are read aloud • Stronger Difference makes the difference clearer and uses only the two clearest kinds • With Sound Hints on, the place that feels different also sounds a little different • Reduce Animation makes broken pieces fade where they are instead of falling. Reduce Motion in iOS Settings is respected too • The whole screen never flashes bright white SOUND • Sounds play along with your music or TV. They don't stop other audio • No sound in Silent Mode. You can play without sound MADE FOR IPHONE HAPTICS • Tact is played by feel, so it is best on iPhone • On devices without haptics, such as iPad, you find the different place by sound (turn the sound on, and turn Silent Mode off) YOURS, ON YOUR IPHONE • No account, and no network connection • Settings and records stay on this iPhone • No ads, no in-app purchases, no tracking Requires an iPhone with iOS 18 or later. Available in English, Japanese, Chinese (Simplified and Traditional), Korean, Spanish, French, German and Portuguese (Brazil).

news.title: Signal restricts mobile screenshots as it confronts ‘existential threat’ of AI surveillance
news.summary: Signal is limiting users' ability to take screenshots in both its Android and iOS apps.
news.body:
Posted:

Signal announced Friday that it’s limiting users’ ability to take screenshots within the secure messaging app — a response to what President Meredith Whittaker described as the “existential threat” of operating systems that integrate agentic AI.

Whittaker wrote that by giving AI agents the ability to “scan” the information on users’ screens, Windows, Android, and macOS/iOS “are undermining Signal’s ability to independently guarantee privacy.”

“Now, in service of AI agentic capabilities, your sensitive data is being captured, stored, and made accessible to whatever local database or remote server an OS-level AI agent is using at that moment,” she said. “All of this is outside of Signal’s control once the data has been captured, and imperils the privacy of all the participants in a conversation.”

Signal already sought to limit these risks by blocking screenshots of its Windows app by default. Now it’s adding similar restrictions in Android and iOS.

That said, users can disable this setting if they wish, which Whittaker said would “break our privacy guarantees.” She also admitted this is an “incomplete” solution, as it doesn’t “address other more sneaky ways AI agents could potentially access application data.”

news.title: Not upgrading to iPhone 18 Pro or Duo? Here’s what’s coming in 2027
news.summary: iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo have been out for quite some time now, and despite that, it’s still incredibly challenging to order an iPhone Duo in a timely manner. If for whatever reason you’re considering skipping out on this year’s iPhones, here’s what you have to look forward to next year. more…
news.body:
iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo have been out for quite some time now, and despite that, it’s still incredibly challenging to order an iPhone Duo in a timely manner. If for whatever reason you’re considering skipping out on this year’s iPhones, here’s what you have to look forward to next year.

2027 is going to be a relatively big iPhone release year for Apple. First, the company will be continuing the iPhone 18 lineup after it introduced a split release schedule . Then, in the fall, the company will debut a new round of flagships in celebration of the 20th anniversary of the iPhone. Here’s what to expect.

For the first time, Apple will be introducing its base iPhone in the spring . Upgrades for the iPhone 18 aren’t quite clear, though more RAM is one of the key rumors. Thermal upgrades will likely happen as well, as well as the new Apple C2 modem.

It’s possible Apple will update the design to fall more in line with the iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro, though we don’t yet know.

This phone will of course equip the A20 chip, and it’ll probably start at the same $899 price point that iPhone 17 currently sits at – after it was increased from $799 in September .

This phone will most likely just end up being a chip bump from the A19 to A20 chip, and debut in the Spring alongside the iPhone 18. Earlier this year, reports indicated that Apple would share many components between the iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e, though it isn’t quite clear what that could mean for the devices.

Out of all of the spring iPhone releases, this one is the one to look forward to. After receiving a lukewarm reception with the initial iPhone Air model, Apple went back to the drawing board and decided to modify the design to fit an ultrawide camera into the device.

Personally, I don’t think an ultrawide camera is too important – though many people will see one camera on the back of the phone and immediately assume it’s less premium, so it’ll probably end up being an important upgrade for the sake of sales. Plus, ultrawide photos can be fun at times.

It should also have a larger battery, reportedly as large as 3500mAh. That’s a roughly 10% improvement from the original iPhone Air. iPhone Air 2 will likely also jump from Apples C1X modem to the C2.

For the 20th anniversary of the iPhone, Apple is expected to debut a fully redesigned iPhone to celebrate. It’ll reportedly be much more glassy , feature significantly slimmer bezels, a quad curved display, and ditch the flat edge design of the iPhone 12 and later.

Personally, I’m slightly skeptical that this’ll truly be a replacement to the “Pro” phone for thermal reasons, but time will tell. iPhone Duo seemingly has strong thermals while not featuring an aluminum unibody, so my concern might not be relevant. It’ll offer two, larger display sizes : 6.4-inch and 7-inch. This largely comes from the bezel reduction.

If you’re holding out for iPhone 18 Pro, this “iPhone 20” is definitely the phone to wait out for.

Lastly, Apple will release a successor to its just-announced iPhone Duo next fall. Of course, you can expect next-generation Apple Silicon with the A21 Pro chip next year, but there aren’t many other substantial changes expected. Apple may bring proper Face ID to the outer display , an improvement from the recently-announced face unlock, but it’s unclear whether this feature will make the engineering cutoff date.

news.title: Here are the top AI agents that can live in your text messages
news.summary: We created a list of the most notable AI agents that can live in your text messages, from general assistants to agents designed for families, travel, and work.
news.body:
Rather than downloading another app, a growing number of agents can simply be texted like an ordinary person.

You text it what you need, and it can remember context, connect to the apps and services you already use, and complete tasks on your behalf. That can mean scheduling an appointment, organizing a calendar, researching a trip, sending an email, making a reservation, shopping online, or reminding you about something days later.

While Instinct is one of the buzziest AI agents at present, thanks to its $10 billion valuation after its latest funding round of $1 billion, there are many others also making a play for this space.

Below are the most notable options so far, from general-purpose personal assistants to agents designed for families, travel, and work.

Ask Proxy ’s biggest differentiator is that it “thinks like a woman,” meaning it aims to anticipate your needs before you even ask, the company explains on its website.

It works like a chatbot you can text like a friend, whether you need gift ideas, help planning an event, or recommendations for things to do that weekend. You can ask it to add important dates to your calendar, set reminders, or help with everyday decisions. You can also send it photos, like an empty table, to figure out how to decorate the table for a dinner party.

Unlike a typical chatbot, Ask Proxy also takes a proactive approach. It can reach out when it notices something you might forget or when it comes across a new activity, restaurant, or experience you might enjoy.

There’s also a work-focused version, which the company explains “gets employees back to work faster, while keeping personal data off company systems.”

The personal version costs $1 per day. For businesses, pricing starts at $15 per employee per month for large companies and $23 per employee per month for small teams with fewer than 49 employees.

Ask Proxy works over SMS. You can text “start” to 820-732-2625.

Caddy is an AI assistant that turns the information scattered across your phone into things you can actually act on. It lives in iMessage for iPhone users and RCS for Android users, so there’s no separate app or inbox to constantly check.

For instance, an email contains an appointment that needs to be added to your calendar or a friend sends a list of things to pick up. Instead of worrying about all the details getting buried, Caddy connects to your calendars and conversations, then identifies things that may require action. It can add events to your calendar, set reminders, keep track of follow-ups, and even do research for you.

Caddy has been available in public beta since April 2026.

Comma is designed to manage tasks across both work and everyday life. Comma carries tasks through to completion, checking its own work and determining when a task is finished.

Completed work is surfaced for review when a decision or approval is needed. It also proactively notifies users and recommends the next steps.

It can work across a user’s browser, computer, and files, while remaining accessible remotely through messaging apps such as Signal, Telegram, and WeChat. Comma maintains context and memory across devices and conversations, and can deliver daily briefings, flag urgent matters, and summarize recorded calls.

Comma is free to start and open source.

Fambot is an AI-powered “chief of staff” for families, designed to bring together the many moving parts of family life, including school communications, sports activities, meal planning, calendars, and other day-to-day responsibilities, and turn them into an organized plan.

The service is designed to work across both an app and text messages. Fambot is available on iOS devices, Android devices, and the web, and families can also interact with it directly over SMS. Every night, Fambot automatically sends a summary of the following day, including upcoming events, to-dos, and details such as school uniform or packing requirements. Parents can reply to those messages to ask questions, check information, or make changes to their calendar.

Fambot currently connects to Gmail, Google Calendar, Outlook, and WhatsApp, with support for Apple Calendar planned for the future.

The company launched in beta in early September 2026 and has raised $3.5 million in pre-seed funding. The service is currently free during the beta period, but Fambot expects to eventually charge roughly the equivalent of a Netflix subscription.

Folk is designed to be an AI assistant you can reach through iMessage, WhatsApp, and Telegram. It can remember personal context, manage reminders, research topics, track flights, handle email, and perform real-world tasks such as restaurant reservations.

One distinction is that Folk runs on its own private cloud computer. It can also run code and execute multi-step tasks rather than merely responding conversationally.

Folk launched its beta in May 2026, and it’s available for free but also offers a Pro subscription for $8.33/month if you want unlimited tasks running in the background.

Haven distinguishes itself by presenting the concept of a “digital twin” rather than merely serving as a text-based AI assistant.

According to the company, Haven understands and adapts to your preferences, routines, and decision-making styles, creating a personalized memory graph based on your interactions. As the company describes , “A personal assistant knows what you asked it to do. Haven knows what you would do and how you would do it.”

Notably, the company envisions future features that customize your experiences across devices, like TV and car.

Currently, Haven is available for free in beta on iPhone and Android devices, and the web. You can also reach Haven by calling or texting (435) 260-6500.

Instinct first made headlines after raising $350 million at a $2.5 billion valuation. In September 2026, it raised $1 billion , valuing it at $10 billion.

The always-available agent can take actions on your behalf, rather than simply answer questions. Users can communicate with Instinct by text or voice and connect it to the apps and services they already use, such as email, calendar, Google Workspace, and more. The company says early users have used Instinct for tasks ranging from planning trips and buying groceries to booking tickets and canceling subscriptions.

In September, Instinct began giving users dedicated email addresses for their assistants. The idea is to let Instinct create and manage accounts on a user’s behalf without filling the user’s personal inbox. The agent can use its address to sign up for services, contact businesses, follow up on requests, and handle tasks that require an email account. (However, this level of autonomy has also raised concerns about privacy and security .) It’s also begun rolling out support for placing calls .

The company remains in private beta.

Powered by Hermes Agent, Iris is designed to let users delegate tasks to an AI assistant directly through iMessage. Users can connect the apps they use and hand over a task with a simple message. The agent then works through the required steps, while retaining relevant context from previous interactions. It’s also designed to follow up with users proactively rather than waiting for another request.

Martin is a general-purpose personal assistant reachable through SMS as well as phone, WhatsApp, email, Slack, and its own iOS app.

It can help manage calendars, email, reminders, tasks, notes, and communications. It can also act on behalf of users by sending messages or making phone calls, while providing daily summaries of what needs attention.

It’s a bit on the pricier side, with subscriptions starting at $21 per month.

Maverick describes itself as an “AI companion who lives in your texts,” acting as a personal assistant that helps manage everyday tasks directly from your messages.

It can fix typos, cancel subscriptions, schedule meetings from voice notes, and help group chats settle on a date for an event. One notable feature is that Maverick asks for your permission before taking action.

The platform also offers hundreds of integrations, including Discord, Gmail, and Slack, allowing it to connect with the apps you already use.

It’s currently in beta and free to use on iMessage. There’s also a Pro version for €27 per month (or approximately $30.25 USD), which includes 500 tasks a month, 20 connected apps, scheduled tasks, and memory.

Miso takes the personal-assistant concept and applies it specifically to travel.

It operates through iMessage and combines AI trip planning with support from a dedicated travel team. Users can arrange flights through messaging while Miso takes into account their travel preferences, loyalty points, and other priorities. Miso also gives travelers access to trip details and flight updates, along with personalized recommendations.

Ohai is another family assistant focused on helping households manage the constant stream of information and tasks involved in everyday family life.

Users can send messages, forward emails, or make voice requests, and the assistant can transform them into schedules, reminders, and plans. It can also coordinate calendars, household chores, and meals across multiple members of a family.

It includes a free basic option, but also offers different subscriptions based on family size, starting at $9.99 per month.

Orbits also has an AI assistant that is focused on the household.

It works through both the Orbits app and text messaging, and can bring together calendars, lists, and conversations while also carrying out tasks for you. That can include searching the web, making purchases, booking restaurants, changing appointments, and requesting quotes for household services.

Additionally, Orbits can remind family members about chores, communicate with service providers, and help coordinate responsibilities beyond the immediate household.

Orbits is backed by investors like Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) Speedrun fund, N49P, and Garage Capital.

Users can interact with Pally as they would with a friend while giving it access to the apps they already rely on. The assistant can connect information spread across services such as WhatsApp, Gmail, calendars, and Google Drive, helping users keep track of plans, receipts, dates, files, and other details.

There’s a free plan available. It works over iMessage, RCS, and Telegram.

Poke launched in March 2026 as a general-purpose assistant that you can reach through text messaging. It can handle tasks involving calendars, planning, health and fitness, smart-home controls, photos, and other everyday activities.

Poke became particularly notable in June 2026 when Apple approved Poke as the first AI agent on the Apple Messages for Business platform. A month later, parent company The Interaction Company of California was acquired by AI coding startup Cognition in a deal valued in the low nine figures.

Rene is an AI personal assistant designed to be a user’s “best contact” rather than another productivity agent. It’s text-based and can turn natural-language conversations into tasks, reminders, summaries, and other follow-up actions. Rene also maintains context across conversations, allowing it to remember details and surface things that may need attention later.

Additionally, it has a browser, can write code, shop for you, as well as create slides and images.

Rene is currently available on iMessage, Telegram, and WhatsApp.

Instead of waiting for users to open an app, Skye is an “ agentic homescreen ” for the iPhone that analyzes information from connected services and surfaces what it thinks is relevant through contextual cards, suggestions, and daily briefings. The assistant can generate audio briefings, prepare information ahead of meetings, surface reminders, and identify potentially useful information.

The company, Signull Labs, raised about $3.6 million in seed funding in 2025. It entered private testing and beta in April 2026, and hasn’t yet announced a public release date.

Stanley is an AI content assistant aimed at content creators rather than general personal productivity. Available through iMessage, Telegram, and the web, it acts as a kind of AI head of content, helping users come up with ideas, turn them into posts, and maintain a consistent publishing schedule.

For instance, Stanley can connect to a user’s Instagram account, using that context to suggest content based on what the user has actually been doing. Users can also send voice notes, which Stanley turns into scripts, captions, and other social assets. It includes a content calendar and can schedule posts, with the broader goal of making content creation a more continuous, automated process rather than something users have to sit down and plan from scratch.

Szn is designed to coordinate tasks and follow-ups through a single conversation thread. Users can send text messages, voice notes, photos, or forwarded emails, and the assistant takes action on their behalf, including making calls, sending emails, and managing follow-ups.

According to the company’s website, Szn has served more than 7,500 businesses across 16 countries, completed over 10,000 jobs, and handled 95 hours of calls.

Tab allows users to delegate everyday tasks through familiar messaging platforms. Users can send requests to the assistant via iMessage or WhatsApp, ranging from ordering groceries to finding birthday gifts, and Tab handles the process on their behalf.

The company emerged from stealth in early October with a valuation of $300 million. Its investors include SV Angel, Valar Ventures, and American Spirit.

The biggest differentiator with Tomo ’s personal assistant for iMessage is that, instead of being a private assistant that only you interact with, Tomo can become part of group conversations.

Also, like other agents, it’s designed to help with goals, accountability, scheduling, and everyday organization. It also has the ability to send reminders, search the web, work with calendars and email, watch videos, and edit photos.

The basic plan starts at $19.99 per month.

Town is aimed more at professional life. It gives users a “Townie,” an AI assistant designed to learn how they work and handle recurring professional tasks. It can work with email, calendars, documents, Slack, and other platforms.

In June 2026, the company raised a $55 million Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz and Forerunner.

Underdog is a privacy-focused AI assistant that launched an invite-only beta in early October 2026. Unlike cloud-based AI services, the model runs entirely on the user’s device, keeping personal data on hardware they already own. The initial release supports Mac and Windows computers, with Linux, iPhone, and Android versions planned for the future.

The company plans to offer the app for free initially and has stated that it will never include advertising.

Wajo ’s first consumer agent, Fo, can call businesses, send emails, join group chats, make bookings and purchases, and coordinate with people to complete everyday tasks.

A key part of Wajo’s approach is giving Fo its own identity. The agent has its own email address, phone number, and payment card, allowing it to interact with businesses without requiring users to hand over their own credentials.

Notably, when Fo encounters something it cannot handle on its own, Wajo says it can bring in a human assistant to finish the task.

Fo launched publicly in September 2026 with a free tier, while heavier workloads and custom agents are available through a paid Pro offering.

news.title: Is selling an AI version of your face to this microdrama startup the future of Hollywood?
news.summary: An actor has licensed his face to a microdrama startup — in a trend that's already popular in China. Experts question the long-term consequences if this becomes a trend in Hollywood, too.
news.body:
For the most part, the content offered by the microdrama startup Shortical is indistinguishable from the rest of its industry . The company produces soapy, melodramatic storylines — almost always risqué romances — that, in bite-sized two-minute episodes, compel viewers to stay glued to their phones so as not to miss the latest twist in a tawdry, cliff-hanger-happy saga.

The primary way that Shortical — which was founded last January — makes money is through subscriptions. Typically, the first 7-10 episodes of a micro-drama are free. After that, if the user wants to finish the series, they have to pay a small monthly fee which unlocks access to all of the site’s content.

Over the past year, the company has churned out a gush of popular live-action romances like “Crossing the Line with My Neighbor,” “Accidentally Married My Boss,” and “Spoiled by My Billionaire Sugar Daddy.”

Lately, however, the company’s homepage is covered in AI-generated content. The reason isn’t exactly hard to figure out: the production overhead for AI content is substantially less than live-action. The profit potential, meanwhile, is substantially higher, if you can draw an audience.

Its latest microdrama premiered in Los Angeles last week. The series, called “Inevitable,” stars Aki Avni, an Israeli film and television star who has been visible in American TV shows for years (he had a stint on Fox’s 9/11-era thriller “24” years ago) but is now trying something largely unheard of in modern Hollywood: licensing his face to Shortical for the sake of its AI content.

The project, which is wholly AI, used Avni’s face to create a digital avatar of him. In “Inevitable,” he plays himself – in a very meta plot in which he — the actor Aki Avni — licenses his face to a film studio, after which thriller-like antics ensue.

This is Shortical’s first foray into such a licensing deal, but it likely won’t be their last.

In a phone interview, Avni told TechCrunch that he found the project both nerveracking and exciting. “Look, it’s a new era for artists,” the actor said. “AI is a new kind of art. It’s a new format. It’s always great to be the pioneer in something.”

Guy Shimoni, the CEO of Shortical, emphasized the creative potential of the new tool. “One of the things that AI does is it enables smaller teams to be able to produce these movie-scale productions,” Shimoni said. “When we were doing mobile-first live action, we were limited by budget, but now we can serve them with epic fantasies. We have kingdoms and dragons. We have superheroes. We have werewolves.”

But AI-generated romances involving werewolves — who, exactly, is watching this kind of thing?

Apparently, a lot of people. While China boasts the biggest microdrama audience globally, Shimoni says that most of his platform’s viewers are actually in the U.S. The industry’s viewer demographic skews heavily female . Many viewers may watch them to wind down at night , getting minor dopamine hits as they drift off to sleep. Many of the AI-generated programs that already exist on the company’s website appear to have millions of views.

Now, Shortical is betting on the creation of a new generation of creators — those who, like Avni, are willing to surrender their likenesses for compensation. “ LICENSE YOUR FACE ” Shortical’s website advertises, explaining that interested parties can submit their social media handles to the company, which will then decide whether to offer them “a contract setting out the terms” of using their persona in the company’s AI-generated content.

A company rep told TechCrunch that this “offering is still in its early days and hasn’t yet resulted in any signed contracts.” They added: “The series with Aki is the first time Shortical has used a real person’s likeness, and it was done through a direct agreement with him rather than through the platform. Shortical hopes the series will draw more attention to face licensing and plans to promote the offering more actively following this launch.”

Much of this trend has already taken hold in China where the microdrama industry originated, where AI-generated content is big, and where face-licensing is already a trend. Although the trend may not be a particularly profitable one for creators. A recent report in Rest of World found that Microdrama firms were paying people “between US$15 to US$700 to license their facial likenesses.”

How much money is Shortical offering for its face-licensing deals? The company isn’t saying. As for if Shortical will offer royalty-based compensation for creators — like the residual system in television, “It’s a case by case [basis],” Shimoni answers vaguely.

A Shortical representative further explained to TechCrunch that the company didn’t want to “share a specific figure” for Avni’s particular contract. However, the person said, he came “on as a partner in the project, and his compensation was in line with industry standards for a comparable non-AI acting role.”

For other actors, however, the deals may be quite different. Plus, many creatives are understandably unsettled by signs of automation creeping into their industry. Until recently, microdramas seemed like a safe, entry-level gateway into the entertainment industry, where young actors could gain experience on sets and hone their craft. Now, companies are downsizing and producing content that doesn’t even require real actors.

Jennifer Cooper, a longtime fan of the industry and founder of the consultancy firm Vertical Drama Love, notes that there’s a lot of distrust of AI — both from audiences and within the microdrama industry itself.

“Everyone’s been impacted by AI,” she said. “A lot of us have either lost work to AI or can see that it’s devastated this industry — [taking microdramas] from something that was a rare thing in the world, that was in growth, and providing work, particularly for young people…[and now] you know, it’s been decimated.”

Questions of consent with AI likenesses have also dogged the industry (some creators claim they have had their likenesses stolen ), which is something that Shortical is obviously trying to address with its new face-licensing endeavor.

Yet these licensing deals could also help to gig-ify the industry, creating a scenario in which creators pay a distributor for the chance to platform their content (or their face), then receive payouts based on the audience engagement they’re allowed to generate. Shortical recently partnered with a company called Payouts.com, which describes itself as a “payout infrastructure platform powering creator and gig economy disbursements at scale.” The plan is to create a system by which creatives can seamlessly interact with Shortical’s platform and get paid.

Cooper believes the push towards AI in the industry is driven by broader financial trends. Most of the microdrama business is led by startups, and VCs love to hear a growth game plan involving automation. “For anyone to get investment at the moment in microdramas, they’ve got to mention the word AI,” she says. “It’s like AI equals gold in everyone’s eyes.”

Despite all the investment in this space, Cooper seems skeptical that there is actually a huge audience for this kind of content. “Some of it does get views. A lot of it doesn’t,” she said, of the AI content. “I think it’s being pushed on an audience more than there is an audience demand or wish for it.”

news.title: Google rolls out new search homepage with AI chat history and no search button
news.summary: Google search is making it even easier to access AI tools on the search page.
news.body:
Google's flagship search experience is evolving into an AI experience with stunning speed. Even time-tested elements of search are getting AI makeovers, and the latest to get this treatment is the search homepage on Google.com. A redesign that's been in testing for the last few weeks is now official, bringing easier access to AI chats and dropping the dedicated search button entirely.

Google search VP Robby Stein confirmed on X that Google is deploying the new desktop search page after a successful test. The page will now have a few more buttons under the search bar, all connected to AI features. There's an image generation button, one for analyzing files, and one for brainstorming with Gemini. The "I'm Feeling Lucky" button remains, but the Google Search button that used to sit next to it is gone.

The search button has obviously been a part of Google's search page forever. However, it wasn't in a very convenient location in the modern interface. When you begin typing a query, the autocomplete suggestions cover that button. You have to click out of the text field to access the button, which is an extra step compared to simply mashing the Enter key to run your search.

news.title: Meta reconsiders 2030 net-zero goal amid record emissions from AI data centers
news.summary: Meta is “re-evaluating” 2030 sustainability goals. Will others follow?
news.body:
Meta’s executives are rethinking the company’s original goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2030. That revelation in Meta’s latest sustainability report comes as the company reported a record percentage increase in greenhouse gas emissions that exceeds any other Big Tech competitor racing to build new AI data centers.

The company’s 2026 sustainability report claims that “our long-term ambitions haven’t changed, but our operating environment has,” according to an introduction from Rachel Peterson, vice president of data centers at Meta, and Blair Swedeen, global head of net zero and sustainability at Meta. In the November 19, 2026, report, they attributed the changing conditions and the need for a rethink to how “demand for AI infrastructure has grown faster than almost anyone projected.”

“We are re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones—including the 2030 timeframe for our net zero emissions goal and our near-term intensity targets—so our approach reflects current operating realities while keeping progress transparent year over year,” Peterson and Swedeen wrote in the report.

news.title: Researcher plants 2m canaries into the AI supply chain. A privacy disaster surfaced.
news.summary: Test using prompts with unique, trackable secrets proves that data doesn't stay private.
news.body:
Researchers planted 2 million digital tripwires in requests sent through a sprawling network of AI services to find out what happened to sensitive information entrusted to them. What they discovered was an ecosystem that leaked highly sensitive data like a sieve.

The exposure was found through an ingenious experiment designed to test if sensitive information can leak through the vast chain of widely used AI services and how that information is exploited when it does. Many of today’s AI apps use services such as OpenRouter or Vercel that act as brokers. These “AI routers,” sometimes also known as “AI gateways,” receive large numbers of prompts sent from AI app end users and route them to an available inference engine based on criteria such as the one charging the lowest price or being best suited for the given task. Instead of using Anthropic, OpenAI, or another big provider, the developer hires an AI router to find the most suitable model.

Update, Nov 21: Posts on both Hacker News and X report that OpenRouter has sent customers an email notifying them that some of their prompts may have been read. OpenRouter cited the research and said that it received a report that the potential exposure involved prompts sent to MiniMax, a China-based model provider. OpenRouter said the researchers' planted URLs were accessed whether the prompts were sent to MiniMax directly or through three other resellers: AtlasCloud, Novita, and StreamLake. OpenRouter has removed a "Zero Data Retention" label from MiniMax-model endpoints. Hat tip: Sulat.com .

Read full article

news.title: Boat Hunter
news.summary: Year 2077. The Atlantic Ocean no longer separates continents. It watches them. For decades, the world learned to smile while sharpening its teeth. Europe and Asia forged an alliance. The American bloc answered with steel, satellites, and fortified trade routes. No one declared open war. No one had to. Peace remained in the speeches, on the screens, and in the treaties. But on the high seas, the truth took another form. The cargo ships never stopped sailing. Food, fuel, minerals, data, weapons—everything kept crossing the ocean under legal flags and flawless orders. Only one thing changed. There are no captains anymore. Now the ships think. Every convoy, every armed destroyer, every autonomous freighter, and every ocean hunter is commanded by artificial intelligences trained to calculate, anticipate, and survive. War no longer needs hatred. It only needs algorithms better than the enemy’s. And you are the finest algorithm ever deployed. You are the most advanced naval combat unit ever built: the fastest hull, the sharpest sensors, the deadliest tactical architecture. You do not sleep. You do not hesitate. You do not forget. Where others detect noise, you see patterns. Where others see waves, you read intentions. Where others react, you have already decided. Your mission is simple to state and nearly impossible to execute: protect your routes, intercept threats, dominate the Atlantic. But the ocean does not forgive mistakes. In its waters travel allies, enemies, and machines that have not yet decided what they will become when the final order arrives. Every radar echo may be a freighter. Every silence may be an ambush. Every encounter may be the beginning of a war the world still insists on denying. There are no heroes here. No parades. No witnesses. Only steel, fog, encrypted signals, and decisions made at the speed of death. On this sea, peace is a display. War is what you are. Welcome to the Atlantic. Enter combat! ---------- Boat Hunter is an accessible naval action and strategy game set in the North Atlantic. You control an autonomous warship on a patrol of consecutive missions, where every decision can put the next operation at risk. MASTER THE OCEAN • Navigate the tactical map, set your heading, and interpret contacts, signals, and radio messages. • Identify allies and enemies: armed ships, merchant vessels, submarines, oil platforms, and floating bases. • Fight at close range with your autocannon and torpedoes. • Repair damage, deploy smoke screens, and decide when to disengage. EVERY MISSION DEMANDS A STRATEGY Reach coordinates, clear hostile sectors, intercept convoys, sink merchant tonnage, defend positions, rescue allies, resupply, and destroy floating targets. Sea conditions, time limits, and enemy behavior will force you to adapt your plans. UPGRADE YOUR SHIP Earn money and score points by completing objectives and sinking enemies. Between missions, upgrade your hull, engine, weapons, damage control, smoke screen, and gunner systems. Higher-quality enemies are more dangerous, but grant greater rewards. Keep your remaining money to begin your next game with an advantage. LEARN AT YOUR OWN PACE A three-mission tutorial teaches you to navigate, aim, and survive. Read the manual and listen to every signal in the sound guide before entering combat. Play visually or through sound and VoiceOver. Choose from three difficulty levels: Deckhand, Captain, and Admiral. Complete as many missions as possible, keep your ship operational, and beat your best score. ---------- This app supports VoiceOver, Zoom, and other iOS accessibility features. If you encounter an accessibility problem, please contact us so we can fix it. Accessibility should be the foundation of a project, not a patch applied to the product.

news.title: Atomicom
news.summary: Space is young, dark and scattered. Atoms drift alone, touching nothing, and in all that emptiness not one thing has ever been built. No water. No stone. No star with a planet worth the name. That is what you are here to change. Atomicom is a puzzle game about binding matter together. Atoms come to you one at a time. Place them on the board, let their loose electrons find a partner, and when every electron in a connected group has one, the molecule is finished: it holds, it leaves the board, and the universe keeps a piece of itself that did not exist a moment ago. HOW IT PLAYS • An atom arrives in the glass cylinder below the board. Take it and drop it on any free square. • Atoms bond with the neighbours above, below, left and right of them. Never diagonally. • A green atom has one electron to give, yellow has two, orange three, red four. Blue atoms give nothing at all: they only take up room you were going to need. • Satisfy every electron in a connected group and the molecule forms and goes. • Run out of squares, or let the cylinder overflow, and the mission ends there. 300 MISSIONS The board starts wide and gets smaller: twelve squares across, then ten, then eight, then a six by six where there is nowhere left to be careless. Every mission asks more than the one before it — more molecules, more obstacles in the way, heavier atoms that need more neighbours before they are satisfied — and every time the board shrinks you begin again at something gentle and climb back up. MADE TO BE PLAYED BY EVERYONE Atomicom is made by Tyflos Accessible Software. Accessibility here is not a switch in the settings, it is how the game is built. • Fully playable with VoiceOver, from the first tap to the last molecule. Nothing has to be seen. • Every square tells you its coordinate, what is on it and how many electrons are still free: "A2, red, 3 free bonds". • The sound tells you where. An atom bonding on the left is heard on the left, and the top of the board sounds higher than the bottom, so the board has a shape you can hear. • Everything that happens without you touching it is spoken: an atom arriving, a molecule finished, a move the rules will not allow and why not. • Vibration answers every move, soft for an atom placed and hard for a molecule completed. • Drag if you like, or tap the atom and then the square. Both always work. • Dynamic Type throughout, and Reduce Motion and Reduce Transparency are obeyed. • Choose your own background, square borders and cylinder colour, and the game tells you when a colour you picked is too faint to make out. ALSO • Play in seventeen languages. • Made for iPhone and iPad. • Your game saves itself: leave in the middle of a mission and pick it up later. • A table of your best games, kept on your device. FREE, AND WHAT COSTS MONEY • The first ten missions are free, with advertising. • "All levels" is a one-off purchase that opens the three hundred. The advertising stays. • "No ads" is a second one-off purchase that removes the banner. It needs "All levels" first. The universe is not going to assemble itself. Start with two atoms.

ALSO • Play in seventeen languages. • Made for iPhone and iPad. • Your game saves itself: leave in the middle of a mission and pick it up later. • A table of your best games, kept on your device.

FREE, AND WHAT COSTS MONEY • The first ten missions are free, with advertising. • "All levels" is a one-off purchase that opens the three hundred. The advertising stays. • "No ads" is a second one-off purchase that removes the banner. It needs "All levels" first.

The universe is not going to assemble itself. Start with two atoms.

news.title: El audio espacial y los auriculares «open-ear» revolucionan la movilidad de las personas con discapacidad visual
news.summary: La unión entre el sonido binaural en 360 grados y los dispositivos de oído abierto resuelve uno de los mayores dilemas de la tiflotecnología. Gracias a este avance, las personas ciegas pueden recibir indicaciones GPS sin aislarse del ruido de la calle. Para una persona ciega o con baja visión, el oído funciona como un […] La entrada El audio espacial y los auriculares «open-ear» revolucionan la movilidad de las personas con discapacidad visual se publicó primero en Conticgo .
news.body:
La unión entre el sonido binaural en 360 grados y los dispositivos de oído abierto resuelve uno de los mayores dilemas de la tiflotecnología. Gracias a este avance, las personas ciegas pueden recibir indicaciones GPS sin aislarse del ruido de la calle.

Para una persona ciega o con baja visión, el oído funciona como un radar constante. Escuchar el tráfico, los pasos o el eco de las paredes resulta vital para caminar con seguridad. Sin embargo, usar el móvil o una aplicación GPS en la calle siempre obligaba a elegir entre dos malas opciones. Podías ponerte ambos auriculares y perder el contacto con el entorno, o llevar solo uno y sacrificar la orientación estéreo. Hoy, la combinación de audio espacial y auriculares open-ear acaba por fin con este dilema.

El audio espacial va mucho más allá del sonido estéreo tradicional. Mediante algoritmos binaurales y sensores de movimiento integrados en los auriculares, el sistema sitúa los sonidos en un espacio tridimensional de 360 grados alrededor del usuario.

Aplicaciones de navegación accesible como Soundscape Community o VoiceVista aprovechan esta tecnología para crear balizas sonoras virtuales. Por ejemplo, si tienes una cafetería o un paso de peatones a tu derecha, escucharás el aviso exactamente desde ese punto. Además, gracias al seguimiento dinámico de cabeza ( head tracking ), si giras el cuello para mirar hacia otro lado, el sonido permanece anclado en la ubicación física real.

La segunda pieza de esta revolución es el diseño de oído abierto ( open-ear ). A diferencia de los auriculares tradicionales de botón o de diadema cerrada, estos modelos dejan el canal auditivo completamente despejado. De este modo, el usuario percibe el sonido digital de su teléfono mezclado de forma natural con el ambiente de la calle.

Actualmente, existen tres formatos principales que compiten en el día a día de la comunidad ciega:

Conducción ósea: Dispositivos como los Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 transmiten el sonido mediante suaves vibraciones a través de los pómulos. Son extremadamente ligeros, resistentes al sudor y dejan el oído libre al cien por cien para la ecolocalización natural.

Conducción aérea direccional (OWS): Modelos como los Cleer ARC 5 , los Bose Ultra Open o los Shokz OpenFit colocan pequeños altavoces justo encima del canal auditivo. Ofrecen una calidad de graves superior y reproducen el audio espacial 3D con mucha mayor precisión.

Intraurales con modo transparencia: Auriculares como los AirPods Pro logran un audio espacial sobresaliente, pero recrean el sonido exterior mediante micrófonos. Aunque resultan muy eficaces, muchos usuarios prefieren la naturalidad de no llevar nada dentro del oído.

El impacto de combinar audio espacial y auriculares open-ear no se limita a los desplazamientos urbanos. En el ámbito deportivo, permite correr o entrenar siguiendo métricas por voz sin perder de vista el entorno.

Asimismo, el sector del gaming accesible está sacando un enorme partido a esta tecnología. Los audiogames y videojuegos con diseño sonoro 3D permiten identificar la posición exacta de enemigos, objetos o puertas mediante el sonido. Con unos buenos auriculares de oído abierto, disfrutar de estas experiencias resulta mucho más cómodo y evita la fatiga auditiva tras varias horas de uso.

Fuentes: Estudio sobre movilidad urbana y audio espacial en discapacidad visual , VoiceVista (ficha oficial en la App Store de Apple) ,

news.title: Top Tech Tidbits
news.summary: Top Tech Tidbits is a free weekly newsletter on access technology for people who are blind, low vision, deaf, hard of hearing, deafblind, neurodivergent and/or disabled. Founded in 2004 and read by over 48,000 people each week, it gathers human-curated news, tips and how-tos every Thursday morning. The app opens the newest issue the moment you open it, and keeps recent issues, and every older issue you open, on your iPhone and iPad, so you can read with no connection. MADE FOR BLIND AND LOW-VISION READERS FIRST • Built for VoiceOver and braille: every section and tidbit is a heading, every control is named, and Apple's accessibility audit checks every main screen in every version. • Larger Text up to the largest sizes, Light and Dark, Bold Text, the Atkinson Hyperlegible font, high-contrast colors and wider line spacing. • Listen: your iPhone reads the issue aloud in the voice and speed you choose, keeps reading when the screen locks, skips a whole section at a time, and stops on a sleep timer. Listen to all your saved tidbits in a row. • "Hey Siri, read me the latest Top Tech Tidbits" and "Hey Siri, search Top Tech Tidbits". • Keyboard commands for a keyboard connected to your iPhone or iPad. EVERY ISSUE SINCE 2008 • Past Issues lists this year's issues, then every earlier year back to 2008. • Search every issue from 2008 to today, tidbit by tidbit, even with no connection, and find tidbits from the iPhone's own search. • Topic Alerts: follow words or names, such as JAWS or braille, and get an alert when a new issue mentions them. Your iPhone looks through the issue itself, so your topics never reach us; only your own Apple devices and your iCloud account have them. • Events lists the upcoming events from the issues, soonest first; add any of them to your calendar in two taps. • A link to an issue, in an email or a message, opens right in the app at the tidbit it points to. • Stories open in Reader View: just their words, without the website's menus and ads. • Translate an issue into another language with Apple's own translation, on your device (iOS 18 or later). KEEP, NOTE AND SHARE • Save tidbits for later, add your own notes, and highlight passages; VoiceOver and braille say where each highlight starts and ends. All of it follows you to your other Apple devices through your iCloud account, with your settings and the place you left each issue. • Share any tidbit with a link that opens the issue right at it, or share a whole issue as a link, a text file or an EPUB book for the Books app or a braille notetaker. • Send Top Tech Tidbits a story from any app's Share button. ALWAYS THE NEWEST • An optional notification each Thursday, normally at 6:00 AM Eastern, with a Listen button; the issue is already downloaded, ready to read. A 1 on the app's icon means a new issue you have not opened yet. • Home Screen and Lock Screen widgets, a Control Center button that starts Listen (iOS 18 or later), and shortcuts on the app's icon. • On iPad, the issue's sections or your saved tidbits sit beside the issue. PRIVACY No account, no advertising added by the app, and no tracking. To learn what readers find most useful the app keeps anonymous counts of which issues and tidbits are opened; you can turn them off in Settings. Details: https://toptechtidbits.com/app-privacy/ Questions and ideas: publisher@toptechtidbits.com

news.title: I Have a Garden
news.summary: One zucchini plant. 48 real days. Here the game's time is your time. You water it tonight and by tomorrow the soil will be a little drier. It gets light and dark at the same time as it does outside your window. The stems, the leaves and the flowers are drawn by an algorithm that imitates how a plant really grows. No two games give you the same shape, or the same harvest. Once you have the zucchini figured out, try the tomato plant: twice the days, up to twenty tomatoes, suckers to prune and a plant that climbs tied to its stake. It brings its own seeds, its own chimera tomato and new achievements. And for a third challenge, the pepper plant: 72 days, and snails that climb the stem to eat its leaves and peppers, which you pick off with your gloves. Each pepper turns from green to yellow to red, and you have to pick it at the right moment. It brings its own chimera pepper, its own seeds and new achievements. You unlock it with a single purchase, which also removes the ads. All three plants grow at the same time, each in its own plot. WHAT YOU'LL DO You check on it, water or feed it if it's time, look for pests and pull the odd weed. For as long as you feel like. HOW THE CYCLE GOES You start by preparing the soil and burying the seed. Until flowering you have to look after it as well as you can, because that stretch decides how many flowers open. When they do, the bees arrive to pollinate them, and if you've kept it up, every one sets fruit. The last stretch takes the most attention: each zucchini has its right moment, and picking it early or leaving it too long costs you points. IMPROVE YOUR PLANT When the cycle ends, you can take the seeds out of the Prime and Overripe zucchini you harvested. There are four qualities: Wild, Adapted, Selected and Heirloom. The better the seed, the more main branches the stem puts out. That raises your chances of getting a chimera zucchini, the hardest thing in the game to pull off. ACHIEVEMENTS There are twenty-seven achievements to earn along the way, gardener's ranks among them: when you gather the harvest you get a score and the rank you earned with the plant. WHAT IT DOESN'T DO No account, no email. No lives, no paying your way forward: the only purchase is the pepper plant, and it's optional. No leaderboard, nobody to beat. And it doesn't message you for the sake of it: a notification arrives when the plant actually needs something, at most one a day, not every evening at seven. It's free and kept going by advertising. If you'd rather support it another way, the pepper purchase removes the ads for good. ALSO You can put a widget on your home screen with the water and feed gauges, without opening the game. A notebook inside that explains every mechanic with real numbers, if you want to know why. A daily graph of water, feed and pests since the day you planted the seed. And a few more surprises. Thank you for playing.
